\section{Complete finite coefficient lists}\label{app:tables}
The two lists below, together with the variable order and evaluation rule, are the complete definitions of $\mathcal P_5$ and $\mathcal R_5$. They are included to make the single-file note independent of an unspecified primitive or a future computation. The JSON files under \texttt{src/\_reference/checks/} contain the same coefficients. The current audit verifies equality of these printed masks with those arrays.

All indices here start at zero. For a list of binary variables $v_0,\ldots,v_{M-1}$ and a hexadecimal integer $q$, write $q=\sum_i q_i2^i$ and define $v^q=\prod_{i:q_i=1}v_i$. The polynomial is the sum modulo two of $v^q$ over the printed list. Thus, for example, the hexadecimal entry \texttt{5} means $v_0v_2$, not the value five. Each listed monomial has coefficient one. There is no coefficient for an unlisted monomial.

\subsection{The 814-term Cartan polarization kernel}
On $[012345]$, concatenate these three lists in their specified order:
\begin{equation}
(v_0,\ldots,v_{29})=
\bigl((z(0ijk))_{1\le i<j<k\le5},\ (x(0ij))_{1\le i<j\le5},\ (y(0ij))_{1\le i<j\le5}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Each parenthesized list is lexicographically ordered. The polynomial is $\mathcal P_5(z;x,y)$ with the identity in Eq.~\eqref{eq:P5identity}. Its evaluation on any other ordered five-simplex uses the induced relabeling. The zero-degeneracy property is a checked polynomial identity.

\subsection{The 3,117-term charge-conjugation polarization kernel}
On $[012345]$, concatenate the following six lexicographically ordered lists:
\begin{equation}
(v_0,\ldots,v_{49})=
\bigl(({\rho_1}(0i))_{i=1}^5,\ ({s_1}(0i))_{i=1}^5,
(x(0ij)),\ (y(0ij)),\ (\widetilde {n_2}(0ij)),\ (\widetilde n'_2(0ij))\bigr),
\end{equation}
where each of the last four lists uses $1\le i<j\le5$, $x=\bar {n_2}$, and $y=\bar n'_2$. Tildes are the actual second binary digits of the signed integer cocycles. The resulting polynomial is $\mathcal R_5({\rho_1},{s_1};{n_2},{n'_2})$ of Eq.~\eqref{eq:R5identity}. No additional quarter-valued, third-digit, or unprinted correction accompanies this list.

\paragraph{Verification.} The independent checker expands each differential on a universal six-simplex, substitutes the cocycle and carry identities, and cancels every squarefree monomial. It also evaluates every degeneracy. The displayed lists and the JSON evaluators agree by the same mask decoding.
